September 2026 (2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30), all shifts. Window coverage: complete.
Contribution margin not set: without an owner margin no lost contribution is priced, so the dollars are paper and machine time.
The supervisor lens: the controllable losses ranked, maintenance and operator downtime, the speed of each wet-end run under its grade's trailing-year speed, shear and dry-end waste.
Side trim and planned maintenance are schedule-driven and listed after, then external downtime (a power outage), which is not controllable.
Shear and dry-end waste are priced in full, all recorded, not over their targets.
Peel and core are controllable too; the roll records carry them, but no lever prices them yet.
Per year at the post's volumes; these name where to look, they do not prescribe a machine adjustment.

How a dollar is priced, for Shear chops (all recorded): 923,124.8 sq ft = 923.125 MSF x $55/MSF paper = $50,772; 923.125 MSF / 5.4 MSF per min = 170.95 min x $1,200/hr machine time = $3,419; contribution: margin not set; per year: x 11.08 (1,800,000 MSF a year / 162,480.957 MSF gross).

Rates: paper $55/MSF (post), machine time $1,200/hr (post), contribution margin not set (assumption: owner to set), trim target 3% (owner, 2026-11-10). Dollars are synthetic records priced at assumed rates (the post's defaults unless changed); they are not a real plant's figures.
Where to look
- The downtime minutes by reason → “Which downtime reason cost the most minutes this month?”
- Side trim, shear and each dry-end reason → “Waste breakdown this month”
- Each grade and web width against its best-fifth speed → “Where is the speed opportunity this month?”
